title: Taxpayer Notification and Privacy Act

claims.claim: Under current law the IRS must notify the taxpayer before making contact with a third party
claims.sourceSpan: before contact is made with such other persons
claims.note: Structural inference: the bill amends the existing 7602(c) third-party-contact notice paragraph (redesignates its subparagraphs), which presupposes an existing pre-contact notice regime.

claims.claim: current law does not require the IRS to spell out the specific information it is seeking
claims.sourceSpan: identifies each specific item of information intended to be sought from such persons
claims.note: The bill adds the specificity duty, implying current law lacked it.

claims.claim: the specificity duty applies when the information relates to determining tax liability, has not been previously requested from the taxpayer, and could reasonably be provided by the taxpayer
claims.sourceSpan: information sought to be obtained from such other persons is related to determining tax liability, has not been previously requested from the taxpayer, and could reasonably be provided by the taxpayer
claims.note: Engrossed adds the 'related to determining tax liability' condition (narrowing the Introduced duty); all three conjunctive conditions present verbatim.

claims.claim: the IRS must identify each specific item of information it intends to seek from the third party
claims.sourceSpan: identifies each specific item of information intended to be sought from such persons

claims.claim: the taxpayer gets at least 45 days to respond before contact is made
claims.sourceSpan: a period of not less than 45 days (or more, if the taxpayer requests additional time and shows reasonable cause) to respond before contact is made with such other persons

claims.claim: one exception applies: the itemized-notice requirement does not apply if the Secretary determines the third-party information is necessary
claims.sourceSpan: Subparagraph (B) of paragraph (1) shall not apply to information sought from a person other than the taxpayer if the Secretary determines that such information is necessary
claims.note: Engrossed exception is a single Secretary-necessity prong scoped ONLY to subparagraph (B) (the specificity duty); the Introduced two-prong carve-out (collection of a tax liability + necessity notwithstanding taxpayer availability) and the (C)-scope clause were removed.

claims.claim: Requires the IRS to tell taxpayers exactly what information it plans to seek from third parties
claims.sourceSpan: identifies each specific item of information intended to be sought from such persons

claims.claim: give them at least 45 days to respond first
claims.sourceSpan: not less than 45 days
claims.note: 'respond' matches source; the Introduced 'including by providing the information described in subparagraph (B)' clause was dropped in Engrossed, so the corrected brief says 'respond' rather than 'provide it.'

claims.claim: Specific Notice Required
claims.sourceSpan: identifies each specific item of information intended to be sought from such persons

claims.claim: IRS must itemize third-party info related to tax liability that the taxpayer wasn't asked for and could provide
claims.sourceSpan: is related to determining tax liability, has not been previously requested from the taxpayer, and could reasonably be provided by the taxpayer

claims.claim: Taxpayers get at least 45 days to respond - more if they request it with reasonable cause
claims.sourceSpan: not less than 45 days (or more, if the taxpayer requests additional time and shows reasonable cause)

claims.claim: Secretary Necessity Exception
claims.sourceSpan: shall not apply to information sought from a person other than the taxpayer
claims.note: Headline changed from plural 'Exceptions' to singular necessity exception - the Engrossed bill adds exactly one new exception.

claims.claim: Itemized-notice requirement waived if the Secretary determines the third-party information is necessary
claims.sourceSpan: Subparagraph (B) of paragraph (1) shall not apply to information sought from a person other than the taxpayer if the Secretary determines that such information is necessary
claims.note: Correctly limits the waiver to the specificity duty (subparagraph (B)); removed the Introduced 'tax collection proceedings' prong that no longer exists in Engrossed.

claims.claim: Names the Act the Taxpayer Notification and Privacy Act
claims.sourceSpan: Taxpayer Notification and Privacy Act

claims.claim: Short-title section - citation name only; no substantive effect
claims.sourceSpan: Short Title

claims.claim: Amends Section 7602(c)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986
claims.sourceSpan: Paragraph (1) of section 7602(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended

claims.claim: to require the IRS to identify each specific item of information it intends to seek from a third party
claims.sourceSpan: identifies each specific item of information intended to be sought from such persons

claims.claim: when that information is related to determining tax liability, has not been previously requested from the taxpayer, and could reasonably be provided by the taxpayer
claims.sourceSpan: is related to determining tax liability, has not been previously requested from the taxpayer, and could reasonably be provided by the taxpayer
claims.note: 'related to determining tax liability' condition added to reflect Engrossed narrowing.

claims.claim: the IRS must, except as otherwise provided by the Secretary, provide reasonable opportunity and a period of not less than 45 days (or more on reasonable cause) to respond before contact is made
claims.sourceSpan: except as otherwise provided by the Secretary, provides the taxpayer with reasonable opportunity and a period of not less than 45 days (or more, if the taxpayer requests additional time and shows reasonable cause) to respond before contact is made with such other persons
claims.note: Corrected detail restores the 'except as otherwise provided by the Secretary' lead-in (a prior material omission) and drops the Introduced 'including by providing the information' phrase that Engrossed removed.

claims.claim: a new exception at Section 7602(c)(3)(B) provides that the itemized-notice requirement (subparagraph (B) of paragraph (1)) does not apply if the Secretary determines the information is necessary
claims.sourceSpan: Subparagraph (B) of paragraph (1) shall not apply to information sought from a person other than the taxpayer if the Secretary determines that such information is necessary
claims.note: Corrected: waiver scoped to specificity duty ONLY (not the 45-day waiting period), and the removed 'collection of a tax liability' prong is gone.

claims.claim: the amendments apply to notices provided under section 7602(c) after the date that is 12 months after enactment
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply to notices provided under section 7602(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 after the date that is 12 months after the date of the enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Section 7602(c)(3)(B) - Secretary's Necessity Exception
claims.sourceSpan: Exception for information specificity

claims.claim: the bill's itemized-notice requirement does not apply whenever the Secretary determines the third-party information is necessary
claims.sourceSpan: Subparagraph (B) of paragraph (1) shall not apply to information sought from a person other than the taxpayer if the Secretary determines that such information is necessary
claims.note: Corrected: scoped to the itemized-notice (specificity) requirement only; the prior 'and 45-day notice' overstatement was removed.

claims.claim: with no standard stated for what makes information necessary and no procedural check on that determination
claims.sourceSpan: if the Secretary determines that such information is necessary
claims.note: Accurate observation of absence - source states no standard or review.

claims.claim: The bill is framed as expanding taxpayer notification rights
claims.sourceSpan: provide for specific taxpayer notice when information is sought from third parties

claims.claim: the necessity exception lets the IRS skip the itemized-notice requirement based on the Secretary's determination that the information is necessary
claims.sourceSpan: Subparagraph (B) of paragraph (1) shall not apply to information sought from a person other than the taxpayer if the Secretary determines that such information is necessary
claims.note: Corrected: no longer claims the 45-day waiting period is bypassed - that overstatement was removed.

claims.claim: with no defined standard, independent review, or notice to the taxpayer that the exception was invoked
claims.sourceSpan: if the Secretary determines that such information is necessary
claims.note: Accurate observation of absence.

claims.claim: Bill gives 45 days to respond but does not specify whether the IRS is barred from contacting the third party if the taxpayer provides the information within the window
claims.sourceSpan: to respond before contact is made with such other persons
claims.note: Source sets a timing floor before contact, not a bar on contact upon early provision - gap holds (the Introduced 'including by providing the information' clause that partly addressed this was dropped in Engrossed).

claims.claim: Bill does not address the taxpayer's right to receive notice that the Secretary has invoked the necessity exception
claims.sourceSpan: if the Secretary determines that such information is necessary
claims.note: Accurate observation of absence.

claims.claim: Adds Section 7602(c)(1)(B): requirement to identify each specific item of information sought from a third party when related to determining tax liability, not previously requested, and reasonably providable by the taxpayer
claims.sourceSpan: is related to determining tax liability, has not been previously requested from the taxpayer, and could reasonably be provided by the taxpayer, identifies each specific item of information intended to be sought from such persons

claims.claim: Adds Section 7602(c)(3)(B): exception that the new itemized-notice requirement does not apply if the Secretary determines such information is necessary
claims.sourceSpan: Subparagraph (B) of paragraph (1) shall not apply to information sought from a person other than the taxpayer if the Secretary determines that such information is necessary
claims.note: New changes entry capturing the added exception (previously uncaptured in changes).

claims.claim: Redesignates subparagraph (B) of section 7602(c)(1) as subparagraph (C)
claims.sourceSpan: by redesignating subparagraph (B) as subparagraph (C)
claims.note: Reclassified the 45-day provision from added to modified: it amends the pre-existing redesignated subparagraph (C).

claims.claim: amends redesignated subparagraph (C) to require, except as otherwise provided by the Secretary, not less than 45 days (or more on reasonable cause) to respond before third-party contact
claims.sourceSpan: except as otherwise provided by the Secretary, provides the taxpayer with reasonable opportunity and a period of not less than 45 days (or more, if the taxpayer requests additional time and shows reasonable cause) to respond before contact is made with such other persons

claims.note: Analytic framing grounded in the necessity exception; correctly scoped to specificity (matches Engrossed).

resolution: Reconciled the analysis from the superseded Introduced (IH, 2025-12-05) text to the re-fetched Engrossed (EH, passed House 2026-04-27) text. Fixes: (1) removed the 'collection of a tax liability' exception prong, which the Engrossed text no longer contains; (2) corrected the (c)(3)(B) exception scope to waive ONLY the itemized-notice/specificity duty (subparagraph (B)), not the 45-day waiting period, in summary, section 2 detail, and underreported; (3) added the Engrossed-only 'related to determining tax liability' condition to the specificity duty across summary, top_lines, sections main, and changes.added; (4) dropped the Introduced 'including by providing the information described in subparagraph (B)' phrase from the section 2 detail and restored the previously-omitted 'except as otherwise provided by the Secretary' lead-in of subparagraph (C); (5) split changes so the new exception is captured under added and the 45-day provision is reclassified as a modification of redesignated subparagraph (C); (6) brief softened 'provide it first' to 'respond first' to match Engrossed; (7) top_lines[1] headline changed from plural 'Exceptions' to the single Secretary necessity exception. gaps[] and likelihoodReason re-verified and unchanged.
notes: Audited against data/bill-text/119-HR-6495.txt = Engrossed in House (EH), 'Passed the House of Representatives April 27, 2026' (2807 chars, 1 page). This ledger REPLACES the prior ledger, which was written against the Introduced text and whose material CONTRADICTED/OMISSION findings referenced Introduced-only clauses ('so much of subparagraph (C) ... as relates to such subparagraph (B)', 'including by providing the information described in subparagraph (B)', 'collection of a tax liability') that do not exist in the Engrossed text. All sourceSpans verified as verbatim substrings of the Engrossed text. featured_quotes/criticisms not judged: no Congressional Record excerpts in scope for this reconciliation pass. Corrected analysis carries zero material errors against the Engrossed text; the one open row is a permissible Zone 3 prognosis.
